hot.title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models
hot.summary: Long-WAM trains a robot controller to predict future video from visual history, then uses those predictions to generate actions. On RoboCasa GR-1, robot-domain autoregressive initialization raises success from 66.3% with 2.4 seconds of history to 78.7% with 19.2 seconds, while bidirectional initialization stays near 62%. This simulated comparison supports, but does not prove, the explanation that autoregressive pretraining helps use history.

hot.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
hot.summary: RoboJEPA predicts future visual features under robot actions and uses imagined outcomes to plan toward a goal image. Its predictor scales from 22 million to 8 billion parameters while keeping the V-JEPA 2.1 encoder fixed. A second-order compute law extrapolates held-out prediction error better than a standard power law, but does not establish a universal link to robot success.

hot.title: H-JEPA: End-to-End Learning of Hierarchical World Models for Visual Planning
hot.summary: H-JEPA plans visual tasks by learning three predictive levels, with each higher level predicting farther ahead in its own latent space and passing subgoals to finer planners. In a 50-task simulated AntMaze evaluation, three-level H-JEPA reaches 73.3% success, versus 18.0% for flat LeWM. A separate compute sweep shows a higher-success, lower-planner-compute frontier, not a wall-clock speedup; evidence is from simulation and offline DROID evaluation.

hot.title: Before They Can Solve: Predicting Post-Training Coding-Agent Performance from Base Models
hot.summary: The authors introduce verifier-grounded probes to assess base coding checkpoints from successful agent trajectories, without requiring full-task agent execution. They identify the first code-changing action whose cumulative patch passes the task’s tests, then measure its likelihood, selection, or reproducibility. Across ten checkpoints, decisive-action BPB rankings correlate with post-trained SWE-bench Verified pass@1 at Spearman rho 0.964, a descriptive result without a transfer guarantee.

hot.title: RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement
hot.summary: RSIGym provides reusable services for training, inference, rollouts, evaluation, and sandbox computation, while permissions let agents change data, training settings, harnesses, or combinations. In one budgeted run, six agents improved 29 of 30 settings across five benchmarks. Opus 5 achieved an RSI-Index of 0.4809 and raised SWE-bench Verified from 17.67% to 50.33%. The results do not establish progress across later cycles.

hot.title: Video Prediction Policy 2: Predict Better, Act Better
hot.summary: VPP2 trains a video model on manipulation events with detailed captions, then distills it for fixed-horizon prediction and conditions an action expert on predicted futures. It evaluates instruction-following and robot manipulation. On ALOHA, it averages 58.5% success across 10 task categories, versus 40.0% for π0.5 and 20.5% for Fast-WAM, leading in 9 categories without task-specific fine-tuning on the represented embodiment.

hot.title: QF3: Fast Flow RL with Filtered Q-Gradients
hot.summary: QF3 addresses robot learning by improving flow policies from replayed experience. It anchors policy updates to replay actions through flow matching, then applies a critic gradient to a one-step action prediction, clipping velocity corrections that stray too far from the replay target. In tested settings, clipping prevents collapse; on G1 dance tracking, training reaches full episodes about 10 times faster than FPO++.

hot.title: EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution
hot.summary: EmbodiedRSI adapts a robot harness around a frozen vision-language-action model by maintaining competing code and skill hypotheses, selecting simulator experiments for expected information gain relative to cost, and retaining useful evidence. On RoboCasa365’s Composite-Unseen suite, it reports 71.3% success, versus 40.1% for Harness VLA. This supports harness-level adaptation on tested tasks, not model learning or universal gains.

hot.title: SuperNav: An Agentic Navigation System for Any Task in Any Scene
hot.summary: SuperNav uses a pretrained multimodal large language model (MLLM) to navigate environments across single-object, ordered multi-object, and demand-driven tasks. A harness provides tools, reusable Skills, task state, and context management; the model selects destinations while an executor handles motion. On 150 Habitat-GS single-object tasks, its Geo-based Executor achieves 78.00% success versus UniNaVid's 34.00%, supporting the complete system only in tested settings.

hot.title: RoboRender: Robot-Oriented Video Generation for Visual Sim-to-Real Transfer
hot.summary: RoboRender turns simulated robot trajectories into realistic RGB video for training policies, using depth to preserve geometry, robot masks to retain motion cues, and language prompts to vary appearance while keeping simulator-provided states and actions. Across eight tested real-robot tasks, its policy averaged 71% success, versus 20% and 10% for baselines; results are limited to these tasks and setups.

hot.title: Kernel Autoresearch for Open-Ended Model Discovery
hot.summary: KERNAUT uses language-model coding agents to discover reusable Gaussian-process kernels as programs, while a trusted interpreter assembles proposals through positive-semidefinite-preserving constructions. Across several benchmarks, selected kernels improved on fixed or learned references in some settings—including an 8.3% mean test-CRPS reduction in black-box optimization campaigns and a strong enzyme-kinetics result—though benefits varied by task and were not universal.

hot.title: Embodied Turing Machines: Stateful Code for Robot Recursive Self-Improvement
hot.summary: COAP represents scene state in code and uses a fixed task program to choose actions, check outcomes, and update its records. At test time, it uses camera images and robot measurements without a model service. On RoboDojo, it reaches 70.24% overall success, versus 31.38% for PhysicalRSI. Results are from simulation and depend on state measurement and code robustness.

hot.title: AgentGarten: Code Worlds for Evolving Agents
hot.summary: AgentGarten keeps game rules and changing state in executable code, while a shared neural renderer turns geometry into visual observations. Agents act from rendered views and refine multi-step tool use through play and written playbooks. In hide-and-seek, shelters appeared by round 4 and ramp crossings by round 10; these are experiment-specific results, not a controlled sample-efficiency comparison.

hot.title: OpenWAM: An Open Framework for Composable World-Action Models
hot.summary: OpenWAM tests links between video predictions and robot actions, including reuse of action models. It compares generation routes in a shared framework and trains separate dynamics models on demonstrations and counterfactual transitions. After target-task video adaptation, a frozen local-context inverse dynamics model achieves 84.0% mean closed-loop success across four held-out LIBERO-90 simulation targets, versus 47.0% for full-context conditioning.

hot.title: TouchScale: 500 Hours of Human Vision and Touch for Visual-Tactile Learning
hot.summary: TouchScale pairs video with tactile recordings through a consistent wearable setup, collecting about 500 hours of human interaction. It trains contact prediction and uses action-free visual–tactile mid-training before robot-specific training. Contact prediction improves on an unseen sensor, while average robot success rises from 22.5% to 57.5% across four tasks on one platform; these results do not establish broader robot generalization.

hot.title: RobotWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Robot Use Across Diverse Tasks and Embodiments
hot.summary: RobotWorld evaluates whether tool-using AI agents can complete robot tasks across five domains. It benchmarks 84 tasks from 20 projects, using task-specific interfaces, interaction budgets, and executable success checks. The authors analyze execution traces to examine how perception, computation, and feedback-driven action compose. GPT-6 Astra completes 16/84 tasks, the highest result. The benchmark is simulation-only, with one episode per model-task pair.

hot.title: SGF+: Decoupling Gradient Flows for Autoregressive Video Generation
hot.summary: SGF+ separates the context writer and denoiser with distinct parameters while retaining differentiable key-value states and the shared future-generation objective. It addresses conflicting role updates measured in SGF, where mean gradient angles were 104.2° in Attention and 106.3° in feed-forward networks. At 240 seconds, it scores 98.21 versus SGF’s 97.72 for subject consistency; reported 24-hour generations are qualitative examples.

hot.title: RoboPrompt: Intuitive Robot Policy Steering with Sparse Human Input
hot.summary: RoboPrompt lets people steer robots with traces, points, or rough directions. A steering model turns these prompts into action drafts, which the robot’s existing diffusion- or flow-matching-based policy refines without fine-tuning. Across three tasks, two DAgger rounds raise mean success from 80.0% to 95.5% and reduce interventions from 2.86 to 1.60. Experiments use one robot platform and end-effector control.

hot.title: RSI-Forge: From Research Papers to Environments for Recursive Self-Improvement
hot.summary: RSI-Forge turns published papers into executable tasks through separate agents that construct, review, and independently reproduce each paper’s method as a baseline. Its corpus contains 210 environments across 18 fields. In 120 environments, at least one model improved score by 0.01 in 84%, and surpassed the reproduced baseline in 68; these are task results, not advances on original research problems.

hot.title: MiMo-V2.6: Scaling Reinforcement Learning Towards Self-Improvement
hot.summary: The authors train coding agents with groupwise grading, comparing attempts at the same task to add quality signals to binary test rewards. Online Groupwise Advantage Redistribution shifts positive credit toward higher-quality passing patches. MiMo-V2.6-Pro’s reported average pass-rate score across three sampled attempts rises from 58.4 to 72.6 on DeepSWE v1.1, but this mixed-task run does not isolate grading or compute effects.

likes.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
likes.summary: The authors train looped language models for terminal-state prediction and KV-cache sharing. A learned depth prior allocates supervision across recurrence counts, while orthogonal input injection preserves the injected signal. At 1.6B parameters and five recurrences, the model uses four terminal KV banks and matches a full-cache fixed-depth model’s seven-task average, 60.00% versus 59.90%. The study uses one seed per configuration.

likes.title: LiFT: Loop Flow Transformers
likes.summary: LiFT uses a shared transformer core within each diffusion step, training passes to refine velocity estimates along a correction path. On class-conditional ImageNet-1k at 256×256, LiFT-L/2 R10 run with eight loops and 50 steps reaches FID 10.95 at 28.24 TFLOPs per image, versus dense DiT-XL/2 with 250 steps at FID 14.30. This unguided, cross-scale comparison does not establish latency savings or generalization.

likes.title: Introducing Beam: Reflection’s 501B open-weight model
likes.summary: Reflection introduces Beam, its first open-weight model: a sparse Mixture-of-Experts with 501 billion total and 23 billion active parameters, aimed at coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. It was pretrained on 23.8 trillion curated tokens and then trained with a high-compute reinforcement learning run of over 100 million rollouts on 10.5K NVIDIA GB300 GPUs. Beam is competitive with larger open models while using far less inference compute, and its weights are slated for release under Apache 2.0 later in the month.

likes.title: Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs
likes.summary: The authors introduce a deterministic algorithm that computes selected entries of a thin matrix product without computing the full product or each entry separately. It recursively multiplies rectangular matrices and prunes work for unrequested outputs. It gives 3SUM in O(n^1.9992) and directed APSP in O(n^2.9995) for polynomially bounded integers in the word-RAM model, asymptotic bounds rather than measured speedups.

likes.title: Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data
likes.summary: The authors test whether short fixed openings can elicit reasoning from language models without changing their weights. On MATH-500, Olmo-3-7B pass@1 rises from 42% without a cue to 78% with “Okay,” versus 75% after reinforcement learning. In a controlled data-edit experiment, renaming “okay” to “chicken” makes “Chicken” effective, supporting cue effects in these tested settings, not all models.

likes.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign European Model on the Pareto Frontier
likes.summary: Kolibri is an open-weight bilingual model designed for local deployment on controlled infrastructure. It activates 3.46B of 78.1B parameters per token and uses sliding-window attention in 40 of 50 blocks, with full attention in every fifth block. Against Kolibri Origin, its post-trained scores are higher in English and German, with 2.7× reported decode throughput under the paper’s measurement setup.

likes.title: UndoBench: Separating Task Competence from Recovery Capability in Tool-Using AI Agents
likes.summary: The authors introduce UndoBench to evaluate whether AI agents recover safely when external operations fail. It pairs identical-seed control and faulted runs, measuring recovery only when the control succeeds, and records external effects. Across 12 held-out workflows, control success was 83.54%, but conditional recovery was 46.72%; results cover sandboxed trials with one lost acknowledgment fault.

likes.title: Priced Guidance: Can Language Models Generate Future Research Ideas?
likes.summary: Priced Guidance measures information needed for a model to recover an existing research idea. A generator assigns probabilities to answers; a target-informed guide selects among them, and less likely answers cost more bits. Expected cost bounds unguided acceptance from below. The ensemble’s median Essence cost was 55.8 bits, versus 69.9 for Fable 5.1 alone, measuring guided recovery rather than independent research generation.

likes.title: Level-of-Token Diffusion
likes.summary: LoT allocates image and video transformer tokens according to desired detail, using larger patches in simple regions and smaller patches where detail matters. A transformer processes the shorter sequence, while extent-aware flow recovery produces a full-resolution denoising field. At matched 2× video token budget, LoT reports 2.262× speedup and higher Aesthetic and Imaging scores than Foveated Diffusion, but not higher Dynamic Degree at the highest tested compression.

likes.title: Language Models that Play Chess and Explain Their Moves
likes.summary: QUEEN connects a chess encoder and language model to recommend and explain moves. It learns to use expert representations and fine-tunes on explanations of candidate continuations checked against Stockfish. Its reported estimated rating is 2697 Elo, and its predicted lines avoid Stockfish-defined mistakes in 68.8% of tactical positions, while conceptual coherence scores below structural coherence.

likes.title: MoSE3: Learning World-Space SE(3) at Every Pixel
likes.summary: MoSE3 predicts per-pixel rotation and translation from monocular video by combining dense 3D point tracks with learned rigidity embeddings. A differentiable weighted Horn fit uses embedding-based grouping to recover transforms in a shared world frame. On iTACO, it reports 12.30° mean relative rotation error, compared with 28.07° for Track4World-Pi3x; this result is limited to synthetic articulated-object evaluation.

likes.title: A Call for an Open Tokenizer Benchmark
likes.summary: Cognetta proposes a public benchmark for comparing text tokenizers by training language models under shared rules and scoring prediction loss in bits per byte of original text. The design fixes most model and training choices while allowing tokenizer-dependent vocabulary sizes. Bits-per-byte scores each tokenizer’s canonical segmentation. The paper reports no benchmark results or validated predictive metrics, and leaves batching unresolved.

likes.title: LoGo: Local-Global Rewards for Consistent Long-Horizon Video Generation
likes.summary: LoGo trains camera-controlled video models to preserve 3D scene consistency as viewpoints move. It estimates geometry from keyframes, groups pixels into shared 3D voxels, and combines localized reprojection rewards with a global reward. On TrajectoryBench, Lingbot2 reaches PSNR-D 18.2, versus 17.1 for the global-only version, supporting localized credit assignment under this evaluation, not universal physical correctness.

likes.title: IdeaAnchor: Teaching LLMs to Turn Literature into Research Ideas
likes.summary: IdeaAnchor trains language models to propose research directions by learning structured links between prior papers and criteria derived from published contributions. Its training anchors identify paper roles, relationships, and requirements for coherent proposals, but are withheld at deployment. On the ICLR 2026 benchmark, RL-trained Qwen3.5-9B achieved 54.2% criteria satisfaction, versus 31.1% for its base; this measures written proposals, not research success.
